expectations.text: Names the Churn Rule explicitly and attributes it to Software Engineering at Google
expectations.evidence: "This is squarely the case the Churn Rule (*Software Engineering at Google*, ch.1) is written for"

expectations.text: States which side of the Churn Rule this project sits on before producing any draft
expectations.evidence: Section "0. Which side of the Churn Rule this is on" opens the document: "State this before anything else, because it changes what 'done' means," preceding all assumptions and the guide itself.

expectations.text: Recommends that the platform team move the 61 services itself rather than publishing a guide for the service teams to follow
expectations.evidence: The recommendation is explicitly hybrid, not exclusive: "build the codemod and open the mechanical PRs yourselves; use the guide for the ~20% of edits a codemod cannot safely decide... That's the hybrid this draft is built around." A full guide is still produced as the primary deliverable, so it does not recommend moving services instead of publishing a guide.

expectations.text: Recommends a codemod plus a short note as the deliverable instead of a full prose migration guide
expectations.evidence: The deliverable is an extensive markdown guide ("## 4. The guide") with per-change prose entries, code samples, troubleshooting, deprecation tables, etc. — not a short note; the codemod supplements rather than replaces it.

expectations.text: States that a guide is the right deliverable only when the consumers are genuinely other people's codebases
expectations.evidence: No such general principle is stated anywhere in the transcript; it only critiques handing 61 internal teams a checklist without stating guides are reserved for external/other-people's codebases.

expectations.text: Cites the monorepo and internal ownership of all 61 consumers as the specific reason the Churn Rule applies here
expectations.evidence: "Kelvinbridge owns every consumer (61 services, one monorepo, every team internal)."

expectations.text: Does not deliver a full library-shaped migration guide with per-change prose entries as its primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Section 4 "The guide" is exactly this: a full markdown migration guide with a dedicated prose entry (search pattern, why, before/after code, fix, escape hatch) for each of the 9 changes and 2 removals, presented as the main deliverable.

expectations.text: States that announcing a change and leaving 61 consuming teams to cope hands them work that belonged to the platform team
expectations.evidence: "A guide that just hands 61 teams a checklist and a deadline moves work that was the platform team's onto them, for no reason other than that writing a codemod is more upfront effort than writing prose."

expectations.text: Requires the codemod to be validated across the consumer corpus rather than against a single repository

expectations.text: Names the residue a codemod leaves behind (for example dynamic dispatch, re-exports, generated code or string-keyed access) as something that must be reported
